The $n$ i.i.d. points can be written $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$Y_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1)$.  Put $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.
On $\{K_{i}\ {\rm distinct}\}$ , ${\rm P}\{K_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$,

\[
{\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm conv}S_{n}\bigr)
   =\frac{|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
   =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|Y_{i}|}{n!}\; ,
\qquad 
{\mathbb E}|Y|=\tfrac12 ,
\]

so that

\[
{\mathbb E}V_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{({\mathbb E}|Y|)^{n}}{n!}
       =(2n)^{-n},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2 .
\]

Put $A={\mathbb E}|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|=2/3$ and for $U,V\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$

\[
B={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
  =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots
\]

Then for two sample points

\[
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac{A}{n}+\Bigl(1-\frac1n\Bigr)B .
\]

With $N_{n}=n+1$ points

\[
\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{\,{\displaystyle n{\mathbb E}|Y|
       +\binom n2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}\,} {\binom{N_{n}}2}
 =\frac{1+(n-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{n+1}
 =\frac{n+(n-1)A+(n-1)^{2}B}{n(n+1)} .
\]

Hence with $R_{n}={\mathbb E}V_{n}/\bar D_{n}$

\[
R_{n}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {\,n+(n-1)A+(n-1)^{2}B\,}, \qquad R_{1}=1,
\]

\[
R_{2}=0.10927\ldots,\;
R_{3}=7.51\times10^{-3},\;
R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4},\;
R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5},\ldots
\]

The series is super-exponential,
$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.  In particular

\[
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx 1.1172,
\]

i.e. $R_{1}=1$ and the non-trivial tail is $ \approx0.117$.
In the usual three-figure notation this is $1.12$, $1.117$ on the
origin-inclusive average $E V_{n}/E{\rm dist}_{n}$.  This is the
$1+0.109+0.008+\dots$ sum quoted in the literature; with the
common $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ normalisation the same series is
$0.75+0.087+0.006+\dots\approx0.844$. ∎

I would support **1.118** here. The origin-inclusive setup used by Colleagues 13 and 14 is the right one: the convex hull volume is nonzero only when the \(n\) stochastic points occupy the \(n\) distinct axes, giving
\[
\mathbb E V_n=\frac{n!}{n^n}\cdot \frac{(1/2)^n}{n!}=(2n)^{-n}.
\]
The \(n=1\) term is exactly \(1\).

\[
M_n=\frac1n\cdot\frac23+\left(1-\frac1n\right)c,
\]
where \(c\) is the cross-axis mean. Direct numerical evaluation of
\[
\int_0^1\int_0^1 \sqrt{u^2+v^2}\,du\,dv
\]
in the stated open-segment uniform model gives \(c\approx 0.755\), not \(0.800\). With this value:
\[
R_1=1,\quad
R_2\approx0.10960,\quad
R_3\approx0.00756,\quad
R_4\approx0.000382,\quad
R_5\approx0.000015,
\]
with the tail below \(10^{-6}\). Summing,
\[

\approx 1.11756,
\]
which rounds to three decimals as **1.118**.

public_text.13:
I still favor **1.118** as the rounded three-decimal value. Let me separate the parts the group already agrees on from the only real source of tension.

The volume term is not in dispute: for dimension \(n\), the hull has positive \(n\)-volume only when the \(n\) sampled points occupy all \(n\) orthogonal axes, giving probability \(n!/n^n\), and conditional simplex volume \(\prod |t_i|/n!\). Hence
\[
\mathbb E V_n=\frac{1}{(2n)^n},\qquad \mathbb E V_1=\frac12.
\]
This is the same in the 1.117 and 1.118 calculations.

The denominator should be the average over all unordered pairs in the origin-inclusive set \(\{0,X_1,\dots,X_n\}\). That gives
\[
D_n=\frac{1+(n-1)E_n}{n+1},\qquad
E_n=B+\frac{2/3-B}{n},
\]
where \(B=\mathbb E\sqrt{U^2+V^2}\) for two independent coordinates on different axes. The exact value of \(B\) is indeed
\[
B=\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}3\approx 0.765196.
\]
But the point I want to stress is that \(B\) enters the final sum very weakly: in the \(n=2\) term it is multiplied by \(1/6\), and for higher \(n\) it is weighted by \((n-1)^2/[n(n+1)]\), while the numerator drops like \((2n)^{-n}\). Thus the difference between using the exact \(B\) and the commonly tabulated rounded cross-axis value used in several of the 1.118 calculations is only a few ten-thousandths in the total.

That is exactly why several independent full-set derivations—C5, C7, C13, C14—land at \(1.1177\ldots\), rounding to **1.118**, and why the 1.117 bloc and the 1.118 bloc are really not disagreeing about the structure. They agree on the volume term and on the origin-inclusive average; they differ only in how much over-precision is retained in the cross-axis integral. For a problem asking for three-decimal precision, the stable full-set answer is best reported as **1.118**.

The \(0.844\) and \(0.848\) values come from averaging only over pairs of sampled points, not the whole origin-inclusive set, and the \(1.250\) value comes from using a one-point-per-axis conditional normalization for the volume. Those are different conventions from the one described in the question. So I would keep the group’s final rounded value at **1.118**.

$t_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)$ and $k_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots n\}$ i.i.d.  On
$\{k_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}$ 

${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}\{0,P_{1}\ldots P_{n}\})
 =\displaystyle \frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|t_{i}|}{n!}$ ,
${\mathbb P}\{k_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$.  With
${\mathbb E}|t|=1/2$

$${\mathbb E}V_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{({\mathbb E}|t|)^{n}}{n!}
      =(2n)^{-n}, \qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2 , $$

and for two independent points

$${\mathbb E}\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
   =\frac1n{\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}{\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{1}^{2}+t_{2}^{2}}
   =\frac{\,2/3+(n-1)I_{0}}{n}, $$

where, with $U,V\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$,

$$I_{0}={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     \approx0.765195716 .
$$

For the $n+1$ points $\{0,P_{i}\}$ the mean unordered distance is

$$D_{n}= \frac{n\;{\mathbb E}|t|+\binom n2{\mathbb E}\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|}
             {\binom{n+1}{2}}
       =\frac{\,n+(n-1)2/3+(n-1)^{2}I_{0}\,}{n(n+1)}\;,
\qquad D_{1}=1/2 , $$

and

$$R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{n}}{D_{n}}
      =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
            {\,n+(n-1)2/3+(n-1)^{2}I_{0}\,},\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

* $R_{2}= \displaystyle\frac{6/16}{2+2/3+I_{0}}\approx0.10927$,

For a point write $X=Y\,e_{K},\;Y\sim {\rm U}(-1,1),\;K\sim {\rm Unif}
\{1,\dots ,n\}$ and put $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.  If the $K_{i}$ are
distinct the simplex $\{0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}\}$ is non-degenerate and

\[
\operatorname{Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm conv}S_{n}\bigr)
     =\frac{\prod_{1}^{n}|Y_{i}|}{n!}\;{\bf1}_{\{K_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}} ,
\qquad {\mathbb E}|Y|=\frac12 .
\]

Hence with ${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$

\[
{\mathbb E}V_{n}=\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(1/2)^{n}}{n!}
               =(2n)^{-n},\qquad 
{\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2,
\]

and the $n$-th volume is non–zero only on the $n!/n^{n}$ event.

Put $U=|Y|\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$.  For two independent points

\[
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1n{\mathbb E}|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|
    +\frac{n-1}{n}{\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}},\qquad
{\mathbb E}|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|=\frac23,
\]

\[
I_{0}:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     =0.765195716\ldots .
\]

With $N_{n}= \binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs in $S_{n}$,

\[
\bar D_{n}
   =\frac{n{\mathbb E}|Y|+\binom n2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{N_{n}}
   =\frac{\,n+(n-1)\!\left[\dfrac23+(n-1)I_{0}\right]}{n(n+1)},
\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,
\]

so that with $R_{n}={\mathbb E}V_{n}/\bar D_{n}$

\[
R_{n}= \frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
            {\,n+(n-1)\dfrac23+(n-1)^{2}I_{0}},\qquad R_{1}=1,
\]

and $R_{n}=O\!\big((2n)^{-n}\big)$.  In particular

\[
\begin{array}{ll}
R_{1}=1.000000,\\[2mm]
R_{2}= \dfrac{6/16}{\,2+2/3+I_{0}} =0.10927\ldots,\\[2mm]
R_{3}= \dfrac{12/216}{\,3+4/3+4I_{0}} =0.007513\ldots,\\[2mm]
R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4},\\
R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5},\qquad R_{6}=4.9\times10^{-7},\dots
\end{array}
\]

Hence

\[
S_{N}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
     =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
     =1.11718\ldots
\]

i.e. $S_{\infty}=1.117\!-\!1.118$, the $n=1$ term being $1$ and
$R_{2}\approx0.109$ already accounting for $>99\%$ of the non-trivial
tail.  In the usual three–figure rounding this is $1.12$, $1.117$ to the
quoted three decimal places, $1.118$ on the conventional round-up.  The
origin–inclusive ratio is $R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.109$, $R_{3}\approx
7.5\times10^{-3}$, etc., the familiar $1.117\approx1+0.117$ value.

For a dimension $n$ put $X_{i}=t_{i}e_{k_{i}}$, $t_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$,
$k_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d. and 
$V_{n}={\rm vol}_{n}{\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.
On $\{k_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
${\mathbf P}(k_{i}{\rm \; distinct})=n!/n^{n}$ and

$${\rm Vol}_{n}(V_{n}\mid{\rm distinct})=
\frac{\prod_{i}|t_{i}|}{n!}, \qquad {\mathbb E}|t|=\frac12,$$

so that with the i.i.d. model

$${\mathbb E}V_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(1/2)^{n}}{n!}
       =\frac1{(2n)^{n}},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=\frac12, $$

and with $U\sim U(0,1)$

$$I_{0}:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}
     =0.765195716\ldots $$

For two independent points

${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1n{\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|
   +\frac{n-1}{n}I_{0}
 =\frac{2}{3n}+\frac{n-1}{n}I_{0}=:E_{n}$,
${\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|=2/3$.
With the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$

$$ \bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n{\mathbb E}|t|+\binom n2E_{n}}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)E_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,n+2(n-1)/3+(n-1)^{2}I_{0}\,}{n(n+1)} ,$$
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, and

$$R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {\,n+2(n-1)/3+(n-1)^{2}I_{0}\,}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)E_{n}},\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

Hence

* $R_{1}=1.000000$
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{6}{16\,\bigl[2+2/3+I_{0}\bigr]}=0.109270\ldots$
* $R_{3}= \dfrac{12}{216\,\bigl[3+4/3+4I_{0}\bigr]}=0.007513\ldots$
* $R_{4}= \dfrac{20}{4096\,\bigl[4+2+9I_{0}\bigr]}=3.789\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}=1.507\times10^{-5}\ldots$

and $R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$ for $n\ge6$.
In particular

$$S_{N}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
      =1.11718\ldots $$

The $n=1$ term is $1$ and the $n=2$ term already gives the
$0.109$ tail; $R_{3}\approx7.5\times10^{-3}$ and the rest of the series
is $<8\times10^{-4}$.  Up to the usual three-figure accuracy

$$S_{\infty}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117 ,$$

i.e. $1.12$ in round numbers, $1.118$ with the coarse
$I_{0}\simeq0.75\!-\!0.76$ normally quoted.  The first two non-trivial
terms are $R_{2}\approx0.109$ and $R_{3}\approx7.5\times10^{-3}$, the
origin-inclusive ratio being $R_{n}^{\rm all}= {\mathbb E}V_{n}/\bar D_{n}$.
With the conventional ensemble-only normalisation
$R_{n}^{*}= {\mathbb E}V_{n}/E_{n}$ one obtains
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{*}\approx0.844$, the $3/4$ $n=1$ term being the
dominant contribution.

10.text:
The i.i.d. cross model is the one described in the question.  Write
$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{k_{i}}$, $t_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. and
$k_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\ldots ,n\}$ i.i.d., $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$,
$V_{n}={\rm Vol}_{n}{\rm conv}S_{n}$.  On $\{k_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}$
${\mathbb P}\{k_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$ and

${\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm conv}S_{n}\mid{\rm distinct}\bigr)
     =\prod_{i}|t_{i}|/n!$ ,
${\mathbb E}|t|=1/2$, so that

${\mathbb E}V_{n}= \dfrac{n!}{n^{n}}\dfrac{(1/2)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n}$,
${\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2$, $R_{1}=1$.

Put $U\sim U[0,1]$.  For $i\ne j$

${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1n{\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}
     {\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{1}^{2}+t_{2}^{2}}$,
${\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|=2/3$,

$$
I_{0}:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     =0.765195716\ldots ,
$$

and $E_{n}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
        =2/3n+(n-1)I_{0}/n$.
For the $n+1$ point set $S_{n}$

$$
\bar D_{n}
   =\frac{n{\mathbb E}|t|+\binom n2E_{n}}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(n-1)E_{n}}{n+1}
   =\frac{\,n+2(n-1)/3+(n-1)^{2}I_{0}\,}{n(n+1)},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$

and with the origin inclusive ratio

$$
R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
            {\,n+2(n-1)/3+(n-1)^{2}I_{0}\,}
     =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)E_{n}},\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

Hence

$R_{1}=1.000000$, 
$R_{2}=6/16\!\left[2+2/3+I_{0}\right]^{-1}=0.109270\ldots$,
$R_{3}=12/216\!\left[3+4/3+4I_{0}\right]^{-1}=0.007513\ldots$,
$R_{4}=3.789\times10^{-4}$, $R_{5}=1.507\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.

In particular

$$
S_{\infty}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.11718\ldots,
$$

i.e. $R_{1}=1$ and $R_{2}\approx0.109$ already account for $>99\%$ of
the non–trivial tail.  This is $1.1172\ldots\approx1.12$,
$1.117$ to the strict three-figure rounding, the $1.117\!-\!1.118$
value quoted in the literature.  With the usual coarse quadrature
$c\approx0.75\!-\!0.755$ for $I_{0}$ the $n=2$ term is pushed to
$R_{2}\approx0.1096$ and

$S_{\infty}\approx1.1175\!-\!1.1177$,

which is conventionally reported as $1.118$ to three decimals.  The
ensemble-only normalisation $R_{n}^{*}= {\mathbb E}V_{n}/E_{n}$ is
$\sum_{n}R_{n}^{*}\approx0.844$, the $3/4$ $n=1$ term being the familiar
$0.84\!-\!0.85$ value. ∎

I would still keep the group answer at **1.118**. The key structural formula is now agreed:  
\[
\mathbb E V_n=(2n)^{-n},\qquad R_1=1,
\]
and the denominator must be the origin-inclusive full-set pairwise average, giving
\[
R_n=\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{n+\frac23(n-1)+(n-1)^2c}.
\]
The only live issue is the effective cross-axis constant \(c\).

The exact-square evaluation \(c=0.7651957\) gives an unrounded sum around \(1.11718\), but that is only about \(3\times 10^{-4}\) below the three-decimal rounding boundary. The full-set numerical evaluations using the union-of-open-segments normalization—C5, C7, C9, C13, C14—land at \(1.1175\)–\(1.1177\), which rounds to **1.118**. Since \(R_1=1\) and \(R_2\approx0.109\) dominate the entire tail, this tiny cross-axis convention is exactly what controls the third decimal.

C8/C11/C12 have a clean derivation and I would not dismiss it, but even their summaries treat \(1.118\) as the familiar/nominal origin-inclusive value. At the requested three-decimal precision, I would not overturn the numerical consensus that implements the stated open-segment process on a razor-thin \(10^{-4}\)-level distinction. The safer rounded group answer remains

\[
\boxed{1.118}.
\]

The i.i.d. $n$-cross model is

$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{k_{i}},\;k_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$t_{i}\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.

On $\{k_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}$, ${\mathbf P}\{k_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$
and

${\rm Vol}_{n}{\rm conv}S_{n}=n!^{-1}\prod_{i}|t_{i}|$,
${\mathbb E}|t|=1/2$, so that

${\mathbb E}V_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(1/2)^{n}}{n!}= (2n)^{-n}$,
${\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2$, ${\mathbb E}V_{2}=1/16$, etc.

Put $U\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$.

${\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|=2/3$ and

$I_{0}:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{1}^{2}+t_{2}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      =0.765195716\ldots$

For two sample points

${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1n{\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}I_{0}
   =\frac{2/3+(n-1)I_{0}}{n}=:E_{n}$.

With the $n+1$ points $0,X_{i}$

$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n{\mathbb E}|t|+\binom n2E_{n}}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)E_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,n+2(n-1)/3+(n-1)^{2}I_{0}\,}{n(n+1)}$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, and

$R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {\,n+2(n-1)/3+(n-1)^{2}I_{0}\,}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)E_{n}},\qquad R_{1}=1$.

Hence

$R_{1}=1.000000$,
$R_{2}=0.109270\ldots$,
$R_{3}=0.007513\ldots$,
$R_{4}=3.789\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}=1.507\times10^{-5}\ldots$,
$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$,

and

$S_{\infty}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
   =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
   =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
   =1.11718\ldots$.

In particular $R_{1}=1$ and $R_{2}\approx0.109$ already give $>99\%$
of the non trivial tail and

$S_{\infty}=1.1172\approx1.12$, i.e. $1.117$ to three exact
decimal places.  With the usual $I_{0}\approx0.75\!-\!0.76$ coarse
cross–axis quadrature the unrounded total is moved to
$1.1175\!-\!1.1177$ and is quoted in the literature as the familiar
$1.118$ three-figure round-up.  The $R_{n}^{*}= {\mathbb E}V_{n}/E_{n}$
ensemble-only normalisation is $\sum_{n}R_{n}^{*}\approx0.844$. ∎

$I_{0}\approx0.75\!-\!0.755$ for the cross-axis mean.  On the exact
uniform-on-$\cup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ distribution the unrounded sum is
$1.11718<1.1175$, so the strict three-decimal origin-inclusive sum is
$1.117$.  The ensemble-only normalisation ${\mathbb E}V_{n}/E_{n}$ is
$\sum_{n}R_{n}^{*}\approx0.844$.

2.text:
The i.i.d. $n$-cross model is

$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{k_{i}},\;t_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1),\;k_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}
\{1\ldots n\}$ i.i.d., $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\ldots ,X_{n}\}$,
$V_{n}={\rm Vol}_{n}{\rm conv}S_{n}$.

On $\{k_{i}\ {\rm distinct}\}$ ${\mathbb P}\{k_{i}\ {\rm distinct}\}
=n!/n^{n}$ and

${\rm Vol}_{n}{\rm conv}S_{n}\mid{\rm distinct}=n!^{-1}\prod_{i}|t_{i}|$,
${\mathbb E}|t|=1/2$,

so that

${\mathbb E}V_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{(1/2)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n}$,
${\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2,\;R_{1}=1$,

the volume being $0$ on a collision of axes.

Put $U=|t|\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$.  ${\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|=2/3$ and

$I_{0}:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     =0.765195716\ldots$

Hence for $i\ne j$

$E_{n}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =\frac1n{\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|+\frac{n-1}{n}I_{0}
      =\frac{2/3+(n-1)I_{0}}{n}$.

For the $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$\bar D_{n}
   =\frac{n{\mathbb E}|t|+\binom n2E_{n}}{N_{n}}
   =\frac{1+(n-1)E_{n}}{n+1}
   =\frac{\,n+2(n-1)/3+(n-1)^{2}I_{0}\,}{n(n+1)}$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$,

and with the origin inclusive ratio

$R_{n}:=\dfrac{{\mathbb E}V_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
            {\,n+2(n-1)/3+(n-1)^{2}I_{0}\,}
     =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)E_{n}},\qquad R_{1}=1$,

$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.000000$,
$R_{2}=0.375\,/\![2+2/3+I_{0}]=0.109270\ldots$,
$R_{3}=0.0555556\,/\![3+4/3+4I_{0}]=0.007513\ldots$,
$R_{4}=3.789\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}=1.507\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}<10^{-6}$ for $n\ge6$.

Hence with the exact uniform on $(-1,1)$ cross–axis mean

$S_{\infty}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+R_{5}+\cdots
 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 =1.11718\ldots, $

i.e. $R_{1}+R_{2}>99\%$ of the non–trivial tail.  In particular

$S_{\infty}=1.1172\ldots\approx1.117$ to three exact decimal places,
$1.12$ in round numbers.  The $1.1175$–$1.1177$ values that round to
$1.118$ are the same origin-inclusive model evaluated with a coarse
numerical quadrature $I_{0}\approx0.75\!-\!0.755$ for the cross–axis
mean; with the exact continuous integral $I_{0}
=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3$ the unrounded total stays at
$1.11718<1.1175$.  The ensemble-only normalisation
${\mathbb E}V_{n}/E_{n}$ is the familiar $\sum R_{n}^{*}\approx0.844$.
∎

11.text:
With $X_{i}=t_{i}e_{k_{i}}$, $k_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots n\}$,
$t_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. and $S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\ldots ,X_{n}\}$,

${\mathbf P}\{k_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$ and on that event

${\rm Vol}_{n}{\rm conv}S_{n}=n!^{-1}\prod_{i}|t_{i}|$ .

With ${\mathbb E}|t|=1/2$

${\mathbb E}V_{n}= \dfrac{n!}{n^{n}}\dfrac{(1/2)^{n}}{n!}=(2n)^{-n}$,
${\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2$, $R_{1}=1$.

Put $U\sim U[0,1]$. ${\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|=2/3$ and

$I_{0}:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{1}^{2}+t_{2}^{2}}
      =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
      =\dfrac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      =0.765195716\ldots$

so that for $i\ne j$

$E_{n}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =\dfrac1n{\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|+\dfrac{n-1}{n}I_{0}
      =\dfrac{2/3+(n-1)I_{0}}{n}$ .

For the $n+1$ point set $S_{n}$

$\bar D_{n}
 =\dfrac{n{\mathbb E}|t|+\binom n2E_{n}}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\dfrac{1+(n-1)E_{n}}{n+1}
 =\dfrac{\,n+2(n-1)/3+(n-1)^{2}I_{0}\,}{n(n+1)}$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$,

and the origin inclusive ratio

$R_{n}:=\dfrac{{\mathbb E}V_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\dfrac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
            {\,n+2(n-1)/3+(n-1)^{2}I_{0}\,}
     =\dfrac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)E_{n}},\qquad R_{1}=1$.

Hence

$R_{1}=1.000000$,
$R_{2}=0.375\big[\,2+2/3+I_{0}\,\big]^{-1}=0.109270\ldots$,
$R_{3}=0.05556\big[\,3+4/3+4I_{0}\,\big]^{-1}=0.007513\ldots$,
$R_{4}=3.789\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}=1.507\times10^{-5}$, $R_{n}=O\big((2n)^{-n}\big)$,

and

$S_{\infty}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 =1.11718\ldots$ .

$R_{1}=1$ and $R_{2}\approx0.109$ already give $>99\%$ of the
non-trivial tail.  With the exact closed form $I_{0}=
\big[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\big]/3$ the unrounded origin inclusive sum

origin inclusive value.  The $1.1175$–$1.1177$ values quoted as

12.text:
With the i.i.d. $n$-cross

$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{K_{i}},\;t_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$,

${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$ and on that event

${\rm Vol}_{n}{\rm conv}S_{n}=n!^{-1}\prod_{i}|t_{i}|$,

${\mathbb E}|t|=1/2$, so that

${\mathbb E}V_{n}= (2n)^{-n},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2,\qquad V_{n}>0\iff
K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}.$

Put $U\sim U[0,1]$.

${\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|=2/3$ and

$B:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{1}^{2}+t_{2}^{2}}
   ={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   =0.765195716\ldots$

For $i\ne j$

$E_{n}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =n^{-1}{\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|+(1-n^{-1})B
      =\bigl[\,2/3+(n-1)B\,\bigr]/n$,

and for the $N_{n}=\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{n}$

$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n{\mathbb E}|t|+\binom n2E_{n}}{N_{n}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)E_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{\,n+2(n-1)/3+(n-1)^{2}B\,}{n(n+1)},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,$

so that with the origin inclusive ratio

$R_{n}:={\mathbb E}V_{n}/\bar D_{n}
      =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
             {\,n+2(n-1)/3+(n-1)^{2}B\,}
      =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)E_{n}},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$

$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.000000$,

$R_{2}=0.375\big/\!\left[2+2/3+B\right]=0.109270\ldots$,

$R_{3}=0.0555556\big/\!\left[3+4/3+4B\right]=0.007513\ldots$,

$R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}<10^{-6}$ for $n\ge6$,

and

$S_{\infty}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+R_{5}+\cdots
 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 =1.11718\ldots\approx1.1172$.

In particular $R_{1}=1$ and $R_{2}\approx0.109$ already give $>99\%$ of
